Definition: from G575 and G2064; to go off (i.e. depart), aside (i.e. apart) or behind (i.e. follow), literally or figuratively:--come, depart, go (aside, away, back, out, … ways), pass away, be past.
BiblicalUsage: To go away, to depart — the Samaritan woman leaving her waterpot and running to the city, Jesus rising early to go apart and pray, Peter running to the tomb and going away wondering, and the promise that one day tears and death and sorrow will depart for good. The word follows people leaving, and it follows sorrows leaving too.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe every departure in this word points to the last one: the day God himself wipes away tears, and nothing that hurts us now is left to come back. Until then, I hold that following Jesus means going where he goes, even when it means leaving the waterpot behind.
